paragraphs.source_en: According to string theory, there is only one fundamental ingredient the string-and the wealth of particle species simply reflects the different vibrational patterns that a string can execute. It's just like what happens with more familiar strings like those on a violin or cello. A cello string can vibrate in many different ways, and we hear each pattern as a different musical note. In this way, one cello string can produce a range of different sounds. The strings in string theory behave similarly: they too can vibrate in different patterns. But instead of yielding different musical tones, the different vibrational patterns in string theory correspond to different kinds of particles.
